deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 56r is Riemann's Latin draft of the curriculum vitae ('Vita') for his doctoral petition to the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty. The next page (56v) drafts the petition letter to the Dean, dated 1 October 1851, and mentions the enclosed dissertation 'in ponendis fundamentis theoriae generalis functionum complexae quantitatis variabilis'. The draft vita says, in order:

(1) Birth: Georg Friedrich Bernhard Riemann was born at Breselenz near Dannenberg on 17 September 1826. He first wrote the year before 'die' and struck it out. His father was Friedrich Bernhard and his mother Charlotte Amalie Ebell; he writes the mother's name as 'Adelgunda Charlotta Amalia e gente Ebelliana'.

(2) Childhood and schooling: he spent his childhood at Breselenz and then at Quickborn. His father held the pastorate of those villages and taught him the first elements of letters. A first opening ('Postquam a patre, qui pagi illius sacerdotium gerebat ...') is crossed out.

(3) Secondary school: at age 14 (1840) he moved to his grandmother ('ad aviam') in Hanover and attended the Lyceum. An interlinear clause gives the reason; its reading is uncertain. Two years later he changed to the Johanneum in Lüneburg.

(4) First draft of the thanks to teachers: the paragraph on the mathematics teachers is drafted twice. The first draft is the pencil passage ending in 'viri optime de me meriti'. It names:
- in Hanover, an artillery captain ('tormentariorum tum centurio'), reading uncertain, 'Wisselius'/'Wiszelius';
- in Lüneburg, Schmalfuss, director of the Johanneum.

(5) Lists of professors:
- 'Illi' (Berlin): Dirichlet, Dove, Eisenstein, Encke, C. G. J. Jacobi.
- 'Hi' (Göttingen): Gauss, Goldschmidt, K. F. Hermann, Lotze, Quintus Icilius, H. Ritter, Stern, W. Weber, Wöhler.
- A struck-out name precedes Goldschmidt (probably Hoeck).
- He gives them 'maximas gratias'.

(6) Second draft of the teachers paragraph, now in the form 'Mathematicorum imprimis studium me tenuit ... magna cum liberalitate atque humanitate me adjuvabant ...'.

(7) University: on their advice, and with his father not unwilling, he entered 'this university' (Göttingen) at the start of the summer semester 1846 with the Johanneum's maturity certificate. He soon gave up theology and resolved to devote himself to mathematics. He spent two years of this period in Berlin and the rest in Göttingen. The sentence 'Doctores habebam illic: Dirichlet' is started again and abandoned, since the list was already written above.

(8) Close: 'Scripsi Gottingae die .. mensis Octobris anni MDCCCLI'. The day is left blank; the petition letter on the next page fills in 1 October 1851.

Roman numerals used: MDCCCXXVI = 1826, MDCCCXLVI = 1846, MDCCCLI = 1851. The page's only role is administrative and biographical, for the doctoral procedure on the dissertation of 1851.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.
The biographical facts agree with the standard accounts (Dedekind's Lebenslauf): born 17 Sept 1826 at Breselenz; Göttingen from Easter 1846; Berlin 1847-1849; Göttingen thereafter.
Stylistically it is an unfinished draft: duplicated paragraphs, the day left blank in the date, and a trailing abandoned sentence ('Doctores habebam illic: Dirichlet').

results.what: Latin curriculum vitae for the 1851 doctoral petition. It gives birth data, parents, schooling (Hanover Lyceum, Lüneburg Johanneum) and the switch from theology to mathematics. It lists his teachers in Berlin (Dirichlet, Dove, Eisenstein, Encke, Jacobi) and Göttingen (Gauss, Goldschmidt, Hermann, Lotze, Quintus Icilius, Ritter, Stern, Weber, Wöhler).
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (autobiographical); its content is known through Dedekind's 1876 biography and the Göttingen promotion files.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely biographical, administrative draft whose facts are well known from Dedekind's biography and the doctoral files. It contains no mathematics.

checkable.asserts: MDCCCXLVI = 1846, the year he entered Göttingen.
MDCCCLI = 1851, the year of the vita and petition.
'quartum decimum annum agens': the move to Hanover was around 1840.
'biennio post': the switch to the Lüneburg Johanneum was around 1842.

transcription_corrections: 'Doctores mihi erant illic: ... ; hic: Gauss' should read 'illi: ... ; hi: Gauss'. The image shows 'illi' and 'hi' (those in Berlin / these in Göttingen).
The struck-out name before Goldschmidt, transcribed '[-Hook[?]-]', is probably 'Hoeck' (Karl Hoeck, Göttingen historian/philologist).

The interlinear clause '{+quum liberis me degere constituisset+}' is uncertain. The image suggests something like 'quum (pater) liberis me erudire/degere constituisset'; it should be flagged as uncertain.
'Wiszelius[?]' looks more like 'Wisselius' in the image; the reading is still uncertain.
The struck-out word after 'Lyceum' is illegible ('[-...-]' is appropriate).
In 'Exacta ibi, deinde Quickborniae' the image has 'deind' with 'e' running into 'Quick-'. The reading 'deinde' is correct.
The mother's given name is written 'Adelgunda' in the manuscript; the transcription is correct here. Standard biographies give Charlotte Ebell.
